_schema.note: Canonical catalog for the racing quiz (racing.html). Edit this file directly and push — GitHub Pages redeploys automatically. Optional live override: set SHEET_CSV_URL in racing.html to a published Google Sheet CSV with the same column names. Specs are researched from real current/recent models but are NOT live-verified against manufacturer spec sheets — treat as a well-informed prototype catalog. Scope (per explicit user decision): road racing + ultra-endurance road cycling (triathlon/Ironman, audax/randonneuring like LEL and PBP, and competitive ultra-distance racing like Race Across America). Trail/mountain-bike racing and dedicated gravel racing are deliberately out of scope — trail racing is planned as its own future category (different bike family entirely: suspension, MTB geometry), and gravel racing overlaps enough with the existing bikepacking catalog to fold in there instead.

fields.name: string — model name shown to users
fields.origin: string — country of the brand, used for the 'prefer Canadian' filter (Cervélo is a real Canadian brand — a nice fit here)
fields.sizes: array of numbers — real frame sizes (cm) this model ships in. Asked directly first (how serious cyclists actually shop); height is only a fallback.
fields.minH: number — cm, fallback height range lower bound
fields.maxH: number — cm, fallback height range upper bound
fields.price: number — face value in whatever 'currency' says
fields.currency: optional string, 3-letter code — omit to mean USD
fields.availability: 'mainstream' | 'boutique' — mainstream: normal dealer network. boutique: smaller/premium, limited distribution (e.g. Pinarello, Colnago, Mason). Scoring favors mainstream by default unless the rider says they're open to boutique.
fields.frameMaterial: 'carbon' | 'aluminum' | 'steel' | 'titanium' — steel/titanium show up mainly among audax/randonneur bikes, where ride comfort and repairability over huge distances matter more than raw weight
fields.groupset: string — the actual drivetrain name shown to users
fields.electronicShifting: boolean — Di2/AXS/EPS electronic vs mechanical cable-actuated
fields.discipline: 'road_race' | 'triathlon' | 'audax' — the primary event/use case this bike is built for. Ultra-distance racing (Race Across America style) is NOT a separate bike pool — it's scored as a strong match against aero road_race bikes and triathlon bikes, and a weak match against audax bikes, since ultra racing is genuinely fast/competitive while audax (LEL, PBP) is deliberately non-competitive endurance riding on similar-looking distances. That distinction is scored explicitly, not treated as interchangeable.
fields.character: 'aero' | 'climbing' | 'all_rounder' | 'endurance' — every bike gets one regardless of discipline (triathlon bikes are always 'aero' by definition, audax bikes are always 'endurance'), but the character QUESTION is only asked when discipline is road_race, since that's the one case where it's a genuine open choice
fields.wheelDepth: 'shallow' | 'deep' — deep-section aero wheels vs lighter shallow climbing wheels
fields.dynamoReady: boolean — commonly built/speced with mounts or hub for dynamo lighting, relevant for all-night audax/ultra-distance riding
fields.image: string — relative path or full URL; leave empty to show the sketch placeholder
fields.retailerUrl: optional string — set ONLY when a human (or an AI agent that actually fetched and read the live page — same rigor, never a guessed/constructed URL) has confirmed it shows this bike. Absent means the result card links to a live search instead.
fields._verified: optional string — present once a bike's data has been checked against a live source rather than general knowledge. States exactly what was confirmed, where, and on what date, and what's still estimated/typical. Entries without this field are the original well-informed-but-not-live-verified baseline described above.
